title: Mastering CBAM Compliance: What SAP’s Latest Release Means for Declarants
summary: Explore how SAP helps EU importers manage CBAM compliance, calculate embedded emissions, and track certificate obligations.
body_markdown:
Under the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), importers of steel, aluminum, cement, fertilizers, electricity, and hydrogen into the EU now face direct legal and financial accountability for the embedded emissions in those products.


Calculate the cost of carbon emissions


[Learn how](https://www.sap.com/products/sustainability/carbon-emissions-calculator.html)


To help them manage it, the latest release of[SAP Sustainability Footprint Management](https://www.sap.com/products/scm/sustainability-footprint-management.html) delivers a CBAM compliance engine for declarants, complemented by[SAP Green Ledger](https://www.sap.com/products/financial-management/green-ledger.html) for liability and asset management.


The urgency is concrete. Starting in February 2027, companies importing goods into the EU will need to buy CBAM certificates, with prices linked to the EU Emissions Trading System and currently ranging between[€75 and €82 per ton of CO₂](https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism/price-cbam-certificates_en) . The first annual reporting deadline is September 30, 2027, covering all imports made since January 1, 2026. This means businesses have less than a year to ensure their often manual and fragmented compliance processes are ready.


In practical terms, carbon is now a priced input for importers, one that directly affects margins, cash flow, and sourcing decisions. The question is whether companies manage that exposure through scalable, auditable processes or continue piecing it together in spreadsheets. ****


## **Inside the October release**


The October release of SAP Sustainability Footprint Management builds out the CBAM compliance and declaration workflow from raw import data to EU registry-ready output.


These existing apps in SAP Sustainability Footprint Management have been extended with CBAM capabilities:


- **Manage footprint inventory scope** now supports adding and managing a dedicated CBAM scope.
- **Import master data** extends to CBAM-relevant business objects, including business partner information tied to non-EU suppliers.
- **Manage location** enables upload and management of supplier locations, a critical foundation for actual supplier emission factors.
- **Import business transactions** introduces a new transaction type for customs import declarations, the foundational data that drives CBAM calculations.


To further streamline CBAM compliance, three new apps handle the core compliance workflow:


- **View default CBAM emission factors** provides access to SAP-maintained content including the EU’s default emission factors, benchmarks, and markups that apply when supplier-specific data is not available. This matters financially. Default values carry a 10% markup in 2026, rising to 20% in 2027 and 30% from 2028.
- **Manage actual CBAM emission factors** is where that penalty gets addressed. Declarants can upload supplier-provided emission factors and use them in place of defaults, directly reducing their certificate obligations and cost exposure.
- **Manage CBAM reports** is the calculation and reporting engine. In a single run, it computes embedded emissions, certificates to surrender, and indicative cost based on date of import at scale. EU registry-ready CBAM declarations are generated instantly with full data traceability, documented calculations, and change logs to support auditability.


Beyond the core applications, the release includes built-in dashboards that surface emissions, certificate requirements, and cost exposure across suppliers and products. And the analytics layer gives companies visibility into where their embedded emissions sit. This intelligence supports not just compliance, but targeted supplier engagement and decarbonization strategy.


## **From emissions to the balance sheet** ****


CBAM creates a new class of financial liability. Every ton of embedded CO₂ in imported goods translates into certificates that must be purchased and surrendered, priced weekly against the EU ETS auction rate. Under both IFRS and U.S. GAAP, provisions must be recognized now for the liabilities arising from CBAM obligations—covering reported emissions and the resulting requirement to surrender carbon certificates, even though cash doesn’t move until certificate purchases begin in February.


The recent integration between SAP Sustainability Footprint Management and SAP Green Ledger for CBAM connects the compliance engine to financial accounting. SAP Green Ledger manages the liability and certificate asset life cycle—from initial exposure recognition through settlement preparation—and creates the entry point for further financial process integration: liability forecasting, margin analysis and simulation, and product costing (planned for 2027). As CBAM expands to cover more products and free allowances phase out, the cost impact will grow. SAP Green Ledger gives finance teams the visibility to protect margins and steer business decisions.


SAP Sustainability Footprint Management quantifies the embedded emissions. SAP Green Ledger turns that into a number your CFO can act on. Together, these solutions help finance teams treat CBAM the same way they do any other managed obligation: planned, measured, settled.


## **What comes next**


In Q1 2027, SAP Sustainability Footprint Management will source customs data directly from SAP Global Trade Services. File upload and API integration are already available now for sourcing customs data from SAP and non-SAP sources.


The broader CBAM picture only intensifies from here. Free allowances under the EU ETS, the mechanism that historically shielded European producers from the full cost of carbon, are being phased out between now and 2034. As those allowances decline, the effective cost of CBAM certificates rises will rise. Also, the scope of covered goods will expand with roughly 180 downstream steel and aluminium products in 2028, with glass, ceramics, chemicals, plastics, and oil refining expected after 2030.


Companies that build their compliance processes on scalable, auditable foundations now will be positioned to absorb those expansions. Companies that do not will find themselves re-engineering under pressure each time the scope widens.


CBAM is not a one-time filing. It compounds in cost and complexity each year.


SAP’s CBAM solution for declarants is available now. To learn more, visit the[Sustainable Finance area of sap.com](https://www.sap.com/products/sustainability/sustainable-finance.html) , explore what the[CBAM definitive regime](https://www.sap.com/blogs/cbam-definitive-regime) means for you, and calculate your CBAM costs using this[calculator](https://www.sap.com/products/sustainability/carbon-emissions-calculator.html) .
